name: Windsor Court Hotel
positioning: The Windsor Court, a downtown New Orleans luxury hotel one block from the French Quarter, entered through a private walled courtyard, with a British and European art collection and mostly suite accommodations
best_for: Art lovers drawn to British painting and royal history
Families and groups who want true suites with separate bedrooms
Travelers who want a quiet base within walking distance of the French Quarter

facts.text: The hotel is in the Central Business District of New Orleans, one block from the French Quarter and the Mississippi River, and within walking distance of the Arts/Warehouse District.
Guests arrive through a private walled courtyard, a pocket of seclusion in the middle of downtown.
Most accommodations are true suites, with an entry foyer, living room and bedroom divided by real walls and doors.
Every room and suite has bedside tables with built-in charging stations and bathrooms in Italian marble.

The Club Level occupies floors 19 through 22, with a dedicated concierge and access to the Club Level Lounge, which serves breakfast, traditional afternoon tea, evening cocktails and hors d'oeuvres, and nightly desserts and cordials.
Spa visits include a plush Italian robe, steam room, infrared sauna and relaxation lounges.
Personalized aromatherapy is included with every massage at the spa.
Afternoon tea is served in Le Salon.
The Polo Club serves classic cocktails with nightly live music.
Pets are welcome, with a $150 per-stay hospitality charge instead of a traditional pet fee.
A complimentary house car is available for drop-offs within a 3-mile limit.

highlights.text: The art collection includes paintings, sculptures, tapestries and furnishings by more than 60 artists from the 17th to the late 20th century; many works are British, with an emphasis on Windsor Castle and the life of British royalty, including originals by William Powell Frith, Sir Joshua Reynolds and Thomas Gainsborough.
The rooftop saltwater pool has private cabanas, is heated for year-round use and is framed by views of the New Orleans skyline.
The James J. Coleman, Jr. Presidential Suite has private terraces, panoramic views across the Mississippi River and the French Quarter, a fireplace, an original Canaletto painting and a private gym.
Many Deluxe and Premium Suites connect to adjoining guest rooms or neighboring suites to create multi-bedroom layouts.
During the holidays the lobby has ten Colorado blue spruce trees and a centerpiece tree with more than 25,000 mini white lights and a toy train circling its base.

considerations.text: The hotel is in the Central Business District, one block from the French Quarter rather than inside it.
Spa treatments should be booked ahead, especially on weekends and during festival weeks such as Jazz Fest, Mardi Gras and the Sugar Bowl.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the hotel's luxury positioning.
